facts.text: Mount Tabor got its name from Plympton Kelly, son of pioneer Clinton Kelly, who suggested the biblical Mount Tabor after reading about Napoleon’s 1799 battle.
The park sits atop a dormant cinder‑cone that erupted over 300,000 years ago as part of Oregon’s Boring Lava Field.
Three historic reservoirs on the mountain were added to the National Register of Historic Places in 2004, preserving their open‑air design.
The reservoirs, threatened by underground storage plans, sparked a decade‑long debate over preserving Portland’s historic open‑air water sources.
Tabor Park’s old plant nursery, once a major supplier of street trees for Portland, is now a historic landmark listed in 2004.
The park’s historic lampposts still draw power from a small on‑site generator, keeping the original lighting alive.
